findings.evidence: Extension.lean:220 `def lift (g : P →ₛₗ[f] Q) : BalancedExtension f P →ₗ[S] Q`, :230 `lift_tmul`, :187 `hom_ext`, :178 `induction_on`, :240 `liftEquiv`.
findings.fix: Define `toQuotient := BalancedExtension.lift g`, where `g : R →ₛₗ[f] U ⧸ I` is `a ↦ a • mk 1`; its semilinearity is exactly `mk_mul_map`. `BalancedExtension.lift_tmul` (`s ⊗ p ↦ s • g p`) then gives `_tmul`, and `BalancedExtension.hom_ext` or `induction_on` simplifies `left_inv`.
findings.issue: `toQuotientBilin`, `toQuotientBilin_apply`, `toQuotient` and `toQuotient_tmul` re-derive the universal property of extension of scalars: they hand-check balancing through `BalancedTensorProduct.lift` and `U`-linearity through `lift_smul_left`.

findings.evidence: Verma/Induced.lean:64-66 `attribute [local instance] LieSubalgebra.envelopingRightModule ... BalancedTensorProduct.leftModule`. The `BalancedExtension` instance already supplies the left action (Extension.lean:135).
findings.fix: Once the general equivalence is restated on `BalancedExtension`, restate `balancedTensorProductEquivVermaModule` and its `_tmul`/`_symm_*` lemmas with `BalancedExtension.tmul`, and drop the local instance attributes.
findings.issue: The Verma specialization states its types on the parallel `BalancedTensorProduct K U𝔟 U K` API and its `local instance` scaffolding (`envelopingRightModule`, `smulCommClass_envelopingRightModule`, `BalancedTensorProduct.leftModule`), not on `BalancedExtension`.

summary: The induced module `U(L) ⊗_{U(B)} R_χ` is extension of scalars along `UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.map R B.incl`, which `TauCeti.BalancedExtension` already provides with its right-module bimodule structure, left `S`-action and universal property. The PR rebuilds that infrastructure on the raw `BalancedTensorProduct` instead of reusing it.
